title: Execution Cascade Mediator — Progressive Result Fencing and Invocation Throttle
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Design and implement an execution cascade mediator to safely chain multiple tool/function calls within a single request stream. Goals: prevent runaway recursion, maintain stream liveness for client-facing streaming responses, support structured output injection from heterogeneous tool adapters, and provide a compatibility shim for older function schemas.
context: We have increased incidents where multi-tool chains (tool A -> tool B -> tool A) produce deep/indefinite invocation loops that leak memory and stall streaming responses. Current mitigations (static max depth) are brittle and break valid patterns that rely on idempotent re-invocation. Additionally, structured output injection from tools with legacy schemas sometimes corrupts the streaming frame boundary, causing frontend deserialization errors.
design_decisions: Introduce a lightweight mediator layer between the orchestration engine and tool adapters that maintains per-request invocation state (flat tokenized ledger) rather than a full call-stack object to limit memory growth.

Progressive fencing: mark tool results as tentative until a commit checkpoint; stream tentative chunks to clients with a deterministic sentinel so clients can render partial output but discard on mediator rollback.

Recursion sentinel: use a combined (tool_id, normalized_args_hash) sliding window and a decaying trust score to detect probable recursion; when threshold crossed, apply a configurable throttle with exponential backoff and optional short-circuit fallback to a safe alternative model variant.

Idempotent injection tokens: require tool adapters to surface an 'inject_token' for structured outputs. Mediator validates tokens against schema compatibility shim; incompatible tokens are converted via best-effort mapping or quarantined into the 'attachments' basket in the final structured response.

Compatibility shim: implement an adapter-level translation registry that maps legacy function response shapes to the current structured-output contract to avoid stream frame desyncs. Registry is pluggable and runtime-updatable via the console.
Telemetry-first: log mediatior events with fingerprints for sampling — include decision reasons (throttle, rollback, schema-translate) to drive future tuning.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike, 1 week): prototype mediator API and tokenized ledger data structure with unit tests. Validate stream sentinel approach with a small synthetic load test.
Phase 2 (engine changes, 2 weeks): wire mediator into orchestration runtime, implement recursion sentinel and exponential backoff policy, add feature flags for progressive fencing.
Phase 3 (adapters, 2 weeks): update canonical tool adapters to emit inject_token and implement compatibility shim mappings for top 5 legacy schemas.
Phase 4 (e2e tests & canary, 1 week): synthetic + production canary rollout on dedicated non-critical tenant, observe stream integrity and latency impact.
Phase 5 (rollback hooks & docs, 2 days): add console controls and runbook; publish design doc and SDK/adapter migration guide.
acceptance_criteria: Must prevent unbounded invocation loops in 95% of synthetic loop scenarios while preserving successful multi-step workflows.
Streaming clients must be able to render tentative frames marked by sentinel without JSON parse errors — verified by integration test harness against two SDK versions.
Telemetry must include a per-request decision trace accessible from Console tracing UI for at least 72 hours in canary region.
Compatibility shim covers top 5 legacy schemas and provides a safe quarantined representation for unknown/unsupported shapes.
Feature flag exists and can instantly disable mediator throttles for emergency rollback without losing in-flight stream liveness.
test_plan: Unit tests for tokenized ledger and sentinel encoding/decoding.
Property tests to ensure ledger memory usage grows sub-linearly with invocation depth when repeated invocations reuse identical normalized_args_hash.
Integration tests with streaming SDK v1 and v2 to assert no frame boundary corruption when adapter translations occur.
Load tests to measure median and 95th percentile added latency from mediator under typical batching; target <5ms median overhead.
Chaos test: inject adapter misbehavior (malformed inject_token) and assert mediator quarantines without stalling the stream.
rollout_plan: Start with internal-only dedicated test cluster + synthetic traffic.
Canary to 1% of hosted traffic for non-SLA customers with streaming enabled (2 days).
Expand to 25% if no regressions (5 days).
Full rollout to dedicated pools after monitoring window and Docs/SDK updates.
